finding.headline: At age 25, the 401(k) limit for 2027 is $25,500, and the IRA limit is $7,500.
details: The IRS says the 401(k) limit rises to $25,500 for 2027, up from $24,500 for 2026, while the IRA limit stays at $7,500.
Social Security benefits grow for each month you delay past full retirement age, and that increase stops at age 70. Your plan to retire at 70 fits this rule.
Medicare starts at age 65, about 40 years from now. Sign up for Medicare at 65 even if you keep working, or your coverage may be delayed and cost more.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.
Your spending now is about $17,389 a year more than your take-home pay, so until you retire the plan takes that from your savings each year. If that is wrong, change your spending now or your pay.
Pay stays at today's level until you retire, with no raises. This is fixed: raises are not certain, so the plan does not count on them. If your pay changes, change it in your answers.
Social Security uses the figure you gave, read as the benefit at 67. Your answers show $2,600 a year from 67. This plan starts it at 62, which pays about $1,800 a year.
If you retire before Medicare starts at 65, health cover costs about $10,000 a person a year until then (an assumption). Other health costs follow CMS figures by age.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. While you work, 401(k) saving comes off taxable pay. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 94. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.
